subject: Computer Networking
title: Network TAPs and Packet Brokers
description: A micro-lesson that makes Network TAPs and Packet Brokers usable.

hook.text: How do you monitor traffic on a wire without disrupting it? Install a TAP — a test access point.

buildup.text: A TAP copies every packet on a link and sends the copy to a monitoring tool. Original traffic flows untouched.

discovery.text: TAPs are passive. They add no latency, don't crash, and can't be detected by devices on the link.

twist.text: Packet brokers aggregate feeds from many TAPs, then filter, deduplicate, and distribute to monitoring tools.

climax.text: Security teams use TAPs for intrusion detection. Network teams use them to troubleshoot performance.

punchline.text: TAPs see every packet without touching traffic. Invisible insight.

quiz.question: Why are network TAPs preferred for monitoring?
options: They copy traffic passively without adding latency or risk
They compress traffic to save storage space

details.summary: Network TAPs are passive hardware devices that create exact copies of traffic flowing through a network link, feeding those copies to monitoring tools without affecting the production network. Packet brokers aggregate, filter, and distribute TAP outputs to multiple monitoring tools efficiently.
details.whyItMatters: TAPs provide guaranteed, unaltered access to every packet on a link. Unlike mirror ports, they cannot drop packets under load, making them essential for accurate security monitoring and compliance.
takeaways: TAPs passively copy all traffic without affecting the live link
Packet brokers aggregate and filter traffic for monitoring tools
TAPs are more reliable than SPAN ports for security monitoring

faq.question: Why use a TAP instead of a SPAN or mirror port?
faq.answer: SPAN ports can drop packets when the switch is under heavy load and may alter frame timing. TAPs are passive devices that copy every packet regardless of load, preserving timing accuracy. For security monitoring where missing even one packet matters, TAPs are the reliable choice.

faq.question: What does a packet broker do?
faq.answer: A packet broker sits between TAPs and monitoring tools, aggregating traffic from multiple TAPs, filtering out irrelevant packets, deduplicating copies, and distributing specific subsets to different tools.
